title: Primary and independent-review provenance

sources.meaning: it was prepared; it was made ready
sources.use: Complete singular prepared predicate. The topic explicitly identifies image, and the subject of preparation is naaltsoos, the output file, not completed artwork. The dictionary is not a software source.

sources.meaning: in place of it; it replaced it
sources.use: This complete singular replacement clause is negated with the general doo…da frame. New and previous target-file referents are supplied explicitly. First nasal a in the postposition carries acute, second does not; both nasal i vowels of hazlį́į́ʼ carry acute. Closing apostrophes normalize to U+02BC.
sources.limits: The source has no explicit file noun. hazlį́į́ʼ is a coming-into-being/spatial form, not a classifying carry verb. The proposal relies on the dictionary’s explicit complete replacement gloss, not an assertion that it is the normal physical handling verb for paper. The application to two digital files and this exact argument sequence are authored and need independent assessment.

sources.meaning: in its place, preposed to replacement/carry-back-in predicate
sources.use: Directly corroborates replacement rather than mere new location. The productive framework also includes a flat-flexible object stem and ł classifier, but the nominated finite sentence does not use a newly derived imperative or handling verb.
sources.limits: The sheep example confirms replacement sense but is not copied as a singular file predicate or used alone to determine argument order. The nominal target before its postposition follows the independent general postposition rule.

sources.use: Temporal adjunct inside target-file relative, locating the target’s presence earlier. Not an adjective meaning old/damaged and not an assertion of present retained bytes.

sources.meaning: a singular flat-flexible object is situated
sources.use: Only the target relative uses this classifying positional state. File/document-as-sheet is the existing project metaphor and has independent modern digital-document corroboration. The target is not called an old image, since staging files can be empty.

Direct primary digital-resource use of the exact relative form siłtsoozígíí. The same opening instructions use Naaltsoos and name a Word document. No claim that a filesystem object is literally flat, or that this assessment gives an overwrite sentence.

Own explicit relative suffix -ígíí and noun-before-postposition rule. The second naaltsoos plus its earlier-presence relative is the immediately preceding nominal target of bichʼą́ąhjiʼ. First Díí naaltsoos refers back to the prepared replacement. This full two-file composition is authored.

Explicit general negative frame, including a did-not past event example. Negates the finite replacement clause. This states factual failed replacement, not a literal modal could-not and not unwillingness or inability attributed to the user.

Paper/document noun and ordinary here/this deictics. Here is the attempted internal destination context, not a claim it is the user-selected provider URI. Díí selects the previously introduced prepared file. Canonical project Eʼelyaaígíí and Naaltsoos bízhiʼ are verified in the current catalogue.

actual_routes.route: ClassicPaintActivity.writeImage -> ImageExporter.encode -> BMP/GIF, DIB, ICO, Base64 or ASCII -> failed rename
actual_routes.evidence: ClassicPaintActivity1363 creates an existing internal staging file with File.createTempFile;1364 calls ImageExporter. Its17-22 routes to each throwing export helper. The external output URI is not opened until1365 after encode returns. All four throw sites occur only after the temporary representation writer returns and closes.
actual_routes.limits: The old staging file may be empty. The target is not asserted to be the selected external URI.

actual_routes.route: ClassicPaintActivity.readImage -> ImportSelection.start -> normalize -> decodeToFile(file,file) -> failed rename
actual_routes.evidence: ClassicPaintActivity1271 creates cached input,1273 fills it,1290 passes it to selection. ImportSelection53 normalizes it;32 passes identical source/destination. TextImageCodec16-18 reads source into temporary bytes,19-22 only checks a signature, then62 attempts replacement.
actual_routes.limits: Preparation may mean unwrapped encoded bytes, not complete pixel decoding.

actual_routes.route: AssemblyActivity.importImages -> ImportSelection.start -> normalize -> decodeToFile(file,file) -> failed rename
actual_routes.evidence: Additional chain independently found. AssemblyActivity235 constructs path;243 successfully ImportFiles.copy writes it;260 passes it to selection. ImportFiles.copy20 opens destination.outputStream before writing. Normalization must then successfully open/read the same existing source before it reaches rename.
actual_routes.limits: Path construction alone does not prove existence; the successful copy and read do. This is separate from AssemblyActivity.makeOutput, which is correctly excluded.

independent_findings.evidence: Independently viewed Wall printed17 both whole page and precise crop: bichʼą́ąhjiʼ is glossed in place of it, and the complete Bichʼą́ąhjiʼ hazlį́į́ʼ clause is glossed it replaced it. Candidate spelling preserves the first acute nasal a and both acute nasal i vowels, removes line-wrap hyphenation, and normalizes apostrophes to U+02BC. This is a finite replacement assertion under negation, not an instruction or a newly generated handling imperative.

Wall printed34 directly gives hashtʼeelyaa, it was prepared; it was made ready. Candidate assigns preparation to naaltsoos and uses the canonical image term as topic. This can cover prepared export bytes or unwrapped image-representation bytes. It does not assert completed artwork, successful save, or full pixel decoding.

The first sentence introduces the prepared file. Díí naaltsoos selects that referent as the next sentence topic/subject. The second naaltsoos plus níwohdę́ę́ʼ kweʼé siłtsoozígíí identifies the previous target, immediately before bichʼą́ąhjiʼ. Young educational grammar printed167–168 explains the relative suffix and postpositions following their related nominal. Combining that rule with Wall’s complete in-place-of replacement clause supports new-file versus old-target order without reversing them. Young–Morgan’s sheep example corroborates replacement vocabulary but, with its different transitive handling predicate and old/new noun sequence, does not independently certify this authored order; it is not the argument-order proof.

hazlį́į́ʼ is not classified here as a flat-sheet handling verb. Its complete dictionary construction has the explicit replacement gloss rather than only a generic location gloss, so using that finite construction for a replacement file is a bounded semantic extension. The cited entry supplies no animate-only restriction. Digital-file nominalization remains authored; no source establishes this entire software sentence or proves it is the standard Navajo filesystem-overwrite idiom.

Wilson printed42 supports níwohdę́ę́ʼ as beforehand/from a previous time. Young–Morgan dictionary4 and7–8 gives the singular flat-flexible stem and siłtsooz positional form. The NMPED source visibly uses siłtsoozígíí for a SharePoint resource and mentions a Word document. That supports the document/file metaphor and exact relative, not an overwrite phrase. The earlier-time adjunct locates target presence before the failed replacement; there is no explicit still-present, nonempty, old-image, retention, recovery or external-provider promise.

Young educational report printed102 explicitly describes doo…da and provides a did-not past-event example; the same page notes time-adverb tense reference. Candidate negates the finite replacement clause. Factual did not replace is a functional paraphrase of the observed failed operation, not a literal translation of English could not and not a claim about the user’s willingness or ability.

caller_review.method: Read production files in the supplied synthetic checkout without changing them; recomputed all104 production SHA256 and Git blob identities and inspected all32 resource-only bridges. The checkout HEAD is synthetic and was not used as current remote authority.
caller_review.export: ClassicPaintActivity1363 creates the existing internal target before1364 ImageExporter.encode. The latter routes BMP/GIF,DIB,ICO,Base64 and ASCII to the four throw sites. Each temporary representation writer returns and closes before renameTo failure. The external URI is opened only afterward at1365. The previous target may be empty.
caller_review.classic_import: ClassicPaintActivity1271–1290 creates and copies the cached input then starts ImportSelection. ImportSelection31–32 and53 normalizes that same existing file; decodeToFile(file,file) reads it, writes and closes unwrapped bytes, then only signature-checks them before the replacement attempt.
caller_review.assembly_import: AssemblyActivity235 alone is path construction, not existence evidence. Successful ImportFiles.copy at243 opens and writes destination.outputStream, and start at260 reaches normalization/read of that file. Thus earlier target existence is established for this separate import route too.
limits: No universal finished pixel decode or encoding claim across all paths.
No present retention claim: temporary output is deleted in finally and import failure can dispose/delete staging.
Destination often means internal staging target, not the selected external URI.
Future callers that pass absent targets require re-review.
caller_review.production_search: Searched main Kotlin/Java for the error key, encode/decode and ImportSelection callers; the inspected routes exhaust the matching production call chain in the104-file authority.

scope_limit: Authored finite digital-file extension at moderate-to-low compositional confidence, not native/runtime/layout certification. No application changes.
